medium_value.description: Define the primary recall estimand explicitly: specify whether PRs or defects receive equal weight, how the two trials are combined, and how missing pairs affect weights. Use that same estimand in the bootstrap, mixed-effects comparison, power simulation and report.

Add explicit outcomes when no candidate N achieves the power target, when fewer eligible fixtures exist than required, or when the affordable N is underpowered. Reconcile those outcomes with G-2 and the requirement for a conclusive answer.

Reconcile the budget formula with the USD 2,500 envelope and enforce the cap before launching work by reserving the maximum remaining liability of active runs. Define how incomplete groups and unspent reservations are handled.

Unify the budget-driven truncation rules with the pre-registered stopping procedure. Specify which analyses remain confirmatory when controls, review-only cells or entire groups are omitted, and prohibit discretionary changes after outcomes are visible.

Add an independent search for defects outside the pipeline-selected fix hunks and incident list, or narrow the primary claim to recall against independently validated known defects. Specify how genuine previously unlabelled findings enter a frozen adjudication process.

Freeze incident collection at a stated timestamp and require a consistent follow-up window across fixtures, or explicitly model unequal observation time. State whether later incidents can appear only in a subsequent sensitivity analysis.

Define what source context annotators and judges may access, provide sufficient head-code context to assess behavior, and isolate their tools from feedback, prior labels and arm identities. Add verification of packet and tool-access boundaries.
Replace the packet requirement that no string from labels or feedback appears with a provenance-based prohibition on copied feedback content, backed by sentinel leakage tests.

Define the judge sampling frame precisely, including uncited findings and labelled defects receiving no finding. Record inclusion probabilities and use a pre-specified weighted estimator with uncertainty for judge-corrected recall and precision.
Resolve the judge sample-size rule for sparse corpora and define how 'partially' maps into each sensitivity. Add blinded duplicate ratings or an adjudication subset to quantify judge reliability.

Specify precision and cost-per-extra-defect formulas, including deduplication across citations, zero-finding runs, repeated trial detections, nonpositive incremental catches and confidence intervals for unstable ratios.

Replace the overlapping YES and NO definitions with mutually exclusive decision criteria tied to practical value. Specify the null hypotheses, multiplicity allocation, precedence rules and an explicit inconclusive region.

Define the positive-control contrast, minimum detectable inflation, uncertainty criterion and fallback for ceiling effects. Separate evidence that oracle material was accessible from evidence that access increased recall.

Add an executable leakage threat model covering network access, repository history, remotes, issue access and local answer-bearing artifacts. Restrict those channels during confirmatory runs or pre-register how detected and undetected exposure limit the claim.

Separate documented prior evaluation exposure from training-contamination risk, and define exclusion versus sensitivity policies for each. Do not treat model availability dates as verified training cutoffs.
Specify model-version pinning, run-order randomization and time blocking across arms and PRs. Record provider identifiers and timestamps and define handling of model-version changes during the study.

Define the 25% exclusion guard's denominator and consequences, minimum valid PR clusters per look, retry eligibility, retry limits and the policy for pairing replacement trials. Preserve failed-run costs in operational cost reporting.

Specify the mixed-effects model's fixed effects, trial treatment, weighting, variance constraints, convergence diagnostics and fallback for singular or failed fits. State whether small-cluster Wald intervals are descriptive or calibrate their coverage.

Define canonical serialization and a reproduction dependency manifest, including container digest, interpreter version, locale, paths, timestamps and floating-point formatting. Distinguish exact artifact reproduction from statistical comparison of fresh live runs.
Create an immutable candidate record branch containing all reproduction inputs before commissioning the reproducer, then publish the final record and archive after reproduction succeeds.

Reconcile the required grader version and freeze its executable hash before confirmatory runs. Define separate versions for union aggregation and the underlying credit rule if retaining the claim that grader 1.3.1 is primary.

Specify a common-fixture comparison policy for frozen c131 and v1 label sensitivities and report their coverage. Do not present unavailable historical label sets for newly seeded fixtures as full-corpus sensitivities.

Validate the complete sequential procedure through simulation, including bootstrap-derived z statistics, actual group sizes, exclusions, both decision boundaries and futility. Derive information fractions from a specified information measure and test the selected alpha-spending implementation against an identified reference.

Define an explicit compatibility and pairing map for the 63 historical runs, preserving their model, label-set and arm distinctions. State which subsets support power estimation and historical placebo calibration.

Define FUTILE and exhausted-budget outcomes as first-class report results and distinguish a completed valid study from a demonstrated positive effect. Make release eligibility depend on completed evidence and honest reporting rather than a favorable or conclusive result.

Report sequentially valid confidence intervals or clearly distinguish fixed-look descriptive intervals from stopping-adjusted inference. Pre-register how estimates and intervals will be reported after an early stop.

Replace the single-shuffle placebo pass requirement with repeated null simulations and pre-specified calibration tolerances for bias, coverage and false-positive rate. Keep a deterministic identical-arm fixture as an exact-zero implementation check.

Specify the permutation exchangeability unit and justify it against the repeated-trial structure. Use PR-level arm swaps when trial differences within a PR are dependent, or demonstrate through calibration that independent PR-by-trial swaps are valid.

Move calibration smoke runs before the final pre-registration hash, then freeze k and the cost policy before confirmatory runs. Define smoke runs as calibration data excluded from inference and resolve the claim that the hash precedes all Phase 1 spend.

Define an enforceable matched-spend policy, including allowable cost imbalance, rounding, cap effects, session overshoot and pair-specific costs. Promote the exact-dollar comparison to the primary analysis if the primary claim remains equal-dollar performance.

Pre-register the model and effort configuration for every phase of every arm and align the single-bare cost with BARE-1's actual model. Either compare the same base model or explicitly describe the experiment as a comparison of model-and-workflow packages.

Model dependence between repeated bare sessions in the power simulation, using empirical repeated-session overlap where available and broad correlation sensitivities otherwise. Simulate the actual selected sequential test rather than only a final-look interval.

Resolve the ordering conflict between the pre-registration hash and k. FR-7 says the hashed PREREGISTRATION.md states 'k per PR', FR-3 says k is fixed 'from the smoke', and G-3/FR-8 require the hash before the first Phase 1 row while placing the smoke inside Phase 1. Pre-register the k formula (cost ratio, rounding, floor 2, cap 30) and the location of the k table; after the smoke, record the realized per-PR k table as PREREGISTRATION-addendum-1.md with its own hash in NOTES, freeze the suite MANIFEST.sha256 only then, and state that smoke spend counts against the cap.

Replace the independence model P = 1 − (1 − p)^k in the power simulation with a correlated-draw model calibrated on the repeated a0_bare trials already present in the 63 runs (per-defect between-trial correlation or a beta-binomial), report power under both models, and draw per-PR defect counts from the candidate table rather than a constant.

State the order explicitly: annotate all candidate fixtures (pr-11, 14, 15, 16 and the sprints 255–265 seeds) first, then run the power simulation and select N using v2 defect counts. Pre-register the rule for fixtures whose v2 defect count is 0 or 1 (excluded, listed with reason). Reconcile G-1 ('every corpus fixture has a v2 manifest') with FR-2 ('for every selected fixture').

Specify the exact commit or tag the reproducer clones (a provisional record branch or tag pushed before reproduction), record its hash in the reproduction report, and state that the report's own commit lands after it. Fix the grader, row and reads code used for regrading to the pin, and require a full regrade of every row with a DEC row if any of that code changes after the pin.

Define the byte-identity contract: list the volatile fields (timestamps, absolute paths, hostnames, durations) that grade.json, rows, reads.md and power.md must not contain, or add a `--deterministic` / canonicalise step and compare canonical forms. Add a bats case asserting two consecutive grades of the same run directory are byte-identical.

Add `in_diff_scope: true|false` to v2 defects (whether the defect lies in or adjacent to lines the PR changed) and pre-register whether out-of-scope incident defects count in the primary denominator (recommended: excluded from the primary, kept as a sensitivity).

State where the `a0_bare_matched` arm and the `bare_sessions` toggle are declared: the cycle suite root under grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0-c132/ or the shipped evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml. If the shipped suite must change, amend G-7's allowlist explicitly with a DEC row.

Route annotator disagreements first to a third blind Opus 5.5 annotator (majority rule), with the lead adjudicating only three-way splits; report the share of defects decided by each path in kappa.json / adjudication.md.

Define the permutation test's exchangeable unit as re-labelling arms among the four cells within each PR (choose 2 of 4 as 'full'), or state why trial i of each arm is treated as a pair; record the number of distinct permutations for the chosen N in reads.json.

Define the cap check as a pre-launch projection (do not start a run if posted spend + in-flight runs × per-run cap would exceed the cap) and state the maximum possible overshoot (concurrency 3 × USD 30) in the pre-registration and the success criterion.

Define `post_cutoff` relative to each model's published training-data cutoff (recorded in fixture.yaml with its source), keep the catalog/availability date as a conservative secondary flag, and re-evaluate pr-11's 'borderline' status under that definition.

Replace the single-shuffle placebo criterion (|Δ| < 0.03, interval covers 0) with a many-shuffle calibration: run ≥ 1,000 seeded within-PR arm permutations through the full pipeline, report the mean placebo Δ (apply the zero band to the mean), the empirical coverage of the 95 % interval (target 0.93–0.97) and the permutation-test rejection rate (target ≈ 0.05). Also state which two arms are shuffled on the 63 existing runs (a0_bare vs a1_full; no matched arm exists there) and under which label set.

Pre-register whether review-catch sandboxes have network during Phase 1. If yes, capture an egress log (hosts contacted) per run in the run directory and have the contamination scan flag any fetch of the repository host; if no, record `network: off` as a took-effect evidence line.

Define 'inside the recorded arm range' for the three live reruns as within the arm's pooled recall interval across PRs (or within ±1 defect of the two recorded trials on that PR), and state that a miss is reported as a discrepancy, not as a reproduction failure.

Order Sprint 1 so the pin-gating harness work (FR-3, FR-11 beads, seeder changes) and the analysis code (FR-5) start first and are reviewed while annotation runs; give Sprint 1 an explicit exit date that leaves the Phase 1 batches (≈ 30 h including smoke, look latency and the open-mount cells) before the credential expiry on 2026-10-28; state the fallback (operator re-auth or a reduced G3) if it slips.

Generate report.md (including the ELI5 numbers and the one-sentence answer) from a template filled from reads.json rather than diffing tables after the fact, so the bats check covers numbers in prose too.

Derive k from a cost model fitted on the cycle-131 a1_full and a0_bare runs by diff size, and use an a1_review_only run (or the first a1_full trial at the pin) as the `oracle_closed` check, so the N × USD 22 smoke full runs are either saved or counted as trial 1; pre-register whichever is chosen.
Weight cells by their defect count in the linear mixed model (or fit on weighted logit-recall) and state it in the pre-registration; report the unweighted fit as a sensitivity.
Pre-register how cost per extra defect is reported when Δ ≤ 0 or its interval covers zero (report 'not defined; Δ interval covers 0' with the Δ interval) rather than a ratio interval.

Add a secondary descriptive read of distinct findings per arm (after `cited_region` dedupe) and strays per arm, so the triage volume produced by k unioned bare sessions is visible next to recall and precision.

Complete the stopping-rule decision logic: (1) define precedence when the YES boundary (Δ > 0) and the NO boundary (Δ < MDE) both fire at one look, or redefine the outcomes as YES-material (Δ ≥ MDE) / positive-below-MDE / NO; (2) change futility to 'conditional power for BOTH answers below 0.20' and state the assumed effect used for conditional power (current estimate vs MDE); (3) define the terminal wording when no boundary fires at the final look ('inconclusive at achieved power X'); (4) give the business interpretation of each of YES / NO / FUTILE / inconclusive; (5) pre-register a bias-adjusted or median-unbiased estimate of Δ to be reported alongside the naive estimate if the rule stops early.

Set a minimum number of PRs (clusters) for any inferential look, e.g. ≥ 6, and re-specify the look schedule for the chosen N (likely two looks for N ≤ 12), using Lan–DeMets to handle the resulting unequal information fractions; state the actual fractions (e.g. 6/10, 1) instead of 1/3, 2/3, 1; define 'information' as cumulative PR count or cumulative defect count explicitly; and use a t-reference with N−1 df (or report that the normal reference is used knowingly) for the z computed from a cluster-bootstrap SE on ≤ 10 clusters.

Record for every v2 defect whether it also appears in the review-derived label set (`in_review_labels: true|false`) and whether the fix commit that produced the hunk was itself a response to the round-1 pipeline feedback (`fix_trigger: review-feedback | incident | other`). Pre-register a sensitivity read restricted to defects whose existence is independent of the pipeline (incident-sourced or fix_trigger ≠ review-feedback) and state in the pre-registration the direction of the residual bias (favours the pipeline arm). Report the share of v2 defects per source in the report's caveats.

Record `incident_window_days_actual` and the packet-generation date per fixture in fixture.yaml and the annotation result; treat fixtures with fewer than 30 days of post-merge history as having a truncated incident source; either generate the incident packets at the latest feasible date or report incident-sourced defect counts per fixture next to the window; add 'incident window per fixture' to the report caveats and to the leave-one-PR-out sensitivity rationale.

State in FR-8 and the pre-registration the model and effort setting inside every arm phase (a1_full REVIEW / AUDIT / dissent, a1_review_only, each a0_bare_matched session, a1_full_openmount), record them per row, and justify any mismatch between the bare sessions (Opus 5.5 --effort high) and the pipeline arm's model. If they differ, either cite the cycle-131 R5 result as the pre-registered justification or add a matched bare arm on the pipeline's model.

Require annotators and the judge to run with filesystem access limited to their packet directory (a fresh temporary directory or sandbox containing only the packets and codebook), log their tool calls, and attach the file-access log to annotation/result.md and judge/result.md as evidence that no label file, feedback file, key.json or arm output was read.

Pre-register a numeric positive-control criterion: e.g. `oracle_exposed_defects` non-empty on ≥ X of the open-mount cells and descriptive Δ(open-mount − full) > 0 on G1, explicitly not an inferential test on 3–4 PRs. Define what 'the apparatus read is void' means for the rest of the report: which reads are still published and under what label ('apparatus unverified').

Pre-register handling of a failed or refused session among the k BARE sessions: re-run that session once (fresh, same k); otherwise grade the completed sessions, record `bare_sessions_completed`, mark the row degraded, exclude it from the primary and keep it in a sensitivity. Add a per-session wall-clock bound for BARE phases and a total bound for the matched run.

blockers.concern: A citation-window grader remains primary despite known ruler effects, and the precision issue is relegated to a Should Have follow-up that may merely document inconsistent rules.
blockers.why_matters: Unioning many bare sessions can increase incidental citation matches or repeated false findings. Apparent recall and precision differences may reflect formatting and deduplication rather than defect detection.
blockers.location: FR-3; FR-4; FR-11 bd-9zmfn; Technical Considerations
blockers.recommendation: Require coherent finding identity, semantic matching, and false-positive accounting before confirmatory grading. Define a pre-registered validity consequence for material grader disagreement rather than retaining a misleading primary solely because it was registered.

blockers.concern: A single random permutation of arm labels is required to produce |Δ| < 0.03 and an interval covering zero. Random relabeling does not guarantee either condition.
blockers.why_matters: Correct analysis code can fail the placebo by chance, encouraging seed selection or changes that force a desired null result.
blockers.recommendation: Use deterministic identical-arm data for exact-zero checks and repeated null simulations for calibration. Pre-register distributional acceptance criteria and prohibit rerolling seeds to pass.

blockers.concern: Budget enforcement occurs after spending exceeds the cap, while concurrency and the prohibition on cutting a started primary group can require further spending.
blockers.why_matters: The stated hard cap and success criterion that spending never exceeds it cannot be guaranteed.
blockers.location: FR-6; FR-8; NFR-5; Scope — Priority order under a lower cap
blockers.recommendation: Reserve worst-case authorized costs before launching runs or groups, include in-flight spending, and stop scheduling when remaining funds cannot cover commitments. Specify whether reserved reproduction and control costs take precedence.

blockers.concern: Fencing untrusted text does not prevent prompt injection, and committing every transcript and credential-adjacent artifact creates an incompletely specified secret-handling boundary.
blockers.why_matters: Issue bodies or transcripts can influence tool-using agents, and credentials or sensitive output can be permanently published on the record branch.
blockers.recommendation: Run annotation and judging with minimal tools and no credential access, enforce role-specific filesystem boundaries, and define redaction and quarantine before records are committed. Test secret scanning with representative credential formats and record redactions explicitly.

blockers.concern: Final percentile bootstrap intervals and permutation p-values are reported without adjustment for the outcome-dependent stopping rule.
blockers.why_matters: Stopping when an effect looks favorable can bias the reported estimate and reduce interval coverage, even if the stopping boundaries themselves are calibrated.
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register sequentially valid inference or an independently validated adjustment for stopped studies. Clearly distinguish nominal fixed-sample summaries from inference that accounts for stopping.

blockers.concern: Fix hunks and recorded incidents still select defects discovered by the pipeline or subsequent maintainers. Relabeling those sources does not discover defects that nobody previously identified.
blockers.why_matters: The proposed independent ground truth can retain the original ascertainment bias and omit genuine bare-only discoveries from recall.
blockers.recommendation: Add independent inspection of complete head changes without feedback-derived candidate selection. Pre-register blinded adjudication of unmatched findings from every arm and distinguish reference-set recall from recall of all real defects.

blockers.concern: Internal sequencing contradiction around k. FR-3 says the pre-registration fixes k per PR 'from the smoke', FR-7 hashes the pre-registration in Sprint 1 before any Phase 1 row, and FR-8 runs the smoke in Sprint 2 after the hash. Either the smoke runs in Phase 0 (violating 'Phase 0 spends no model money' and giving the lead a look at a1_full performance on the new corpus before locking the plan) or k is set after the hash, which guarantees an addendum and leaves a free parameter in the primary contrast.
blockers.why_matters: k determines the matched arm's recall directly (P ≈ 1 − (1 − p)^k). A degree of freedom chosen after seeing smoke results undermines the pre-registration the entire proof structure rests on, and the hash in MANIFEST would attest to a document that does not yet contain the decisive parameter.
blockers.location: FR-3 (k derivation), FR-7 (hash before first row), FR-8 (smoke first, k derived and recorded), § Constraints 'Phase 0 spends no model money'
blockers.recommendation: Choose one: (a) pre-register a deterministic k formula using only the 63 existing runs' cost ratios and the PR diff size, with the smoke serving only to verify the formula within a declared tolerance; or (b) explicitly make the smoke a pre-registration input, run it before hashing, budget it under Phase 0 and state that the lead sees smoke grades. Record which option in a DEC row and remove the contradiction from FR-3/FR-8.

blockers.concern: Model availability dates are used as post-cutoff evidence, although availability does not establish a model's training cutoff or absence of later retrieval and exposure.
blockers.why_matters: The study can claim unseen evaluation without evidence that the models lacked access to the fixes or prior public reviews.
blockers.recommendation: Separate publication timing, known training cutoff, prior evaluation exposure, and runtime access. Mark unknown training exposure explicitly and restrict the unseen claim to what the evidence supports.

blockers.concern: Pairwise exclusions can remove expensive or unsuccessful runs from both effectiveness and cost summaries, and the 25% guard and optional replacement trials lack explicit scope and rules.
blockers.why_matters: An arm that fails more often can appear more effective or economical when only completed clean pairs are analyzed.
blockers.location: FR-5(g); FR-8; Risks & Mitigation — refusal fallbacks
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register arm-level failure reporting, total attempted spending, replacement rules, and the exact 25% denominator and consequence. Include an operational sensitivity counting failed attempts and their costs.

blockers.concern: The 're-derived' ground truth is still downstream of the pipeline. FR-1 defines fix = 'the commit that closed the feedback', so every fix-commit hunk is a response to the pipeline's own round-1 review/audit findings. Defects the pipeline missed and nobody fixed never appear in head..fix. The only channel that could surface them is the incident packet, but it is bounded to 30 days after merge and the newest fixtures (sprints 263-265) merged 2026-10-14 to 10-20, so their incident history is essentially empty. The PRD's central claim that labels are now independent of the pipeline is not met by this design.
blockers.why_matters: The whole cycle exists to remove the label circularity named in the Problem Statement ('a bare arm cannot be credited for a real defect the pipeline missed'). If the v2 labels are mostly pipeline-actioned fixes under a new label_source name, the primary Δ inherits the same bias toward the pipeline and the report would present it as settled. A consortium reader who notices that fix = closed-feedback commit will reject the headline.
blockers.location: FR-1 (record-pairs fix column), FR-2 (label_source fix-commit), Problem Statement § User Pain Points bullet 2, G-1, Appendix A 'Label source'
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register and report the share of v2 defects whose fix hunk maps to a round-1 feedback item (traceable from the feedback files the packets exclude); label those `fix-commit:feedback-actioned` and the rest `fix-commit:unprompted`. Add at least one label channel that is not a pipeline response: extend the later-fix window to the present day for every fixture, include fixes landed in any later cycle touching the head-changed files, and add a blind defect hunt by a model family used in no arm as a third annotator source. Reword the report claim from 'independent of the pipeline' to the measured independence share, and include a sensitivity restricted to unprompted/incident defects only.

blockers.concern: The YES and NO stopping criteria overlap: YES tests whether Δ exceeds zero, while NO tests whether Δ is below 0.10. A true effect between zero and 0.10 can support both conclusions.
blockers.why_matters: The study can issue contradictory operational recommendations even when its estimates are accurate.
blockers.recommendation: Define mutually interpretable conclusions, such as positive benefit, benefit smaller than the practical threshold, and inconclusive. Specify hypothesis families, error allocation, simultaneous-boundary precedence, and the recommendation for effects between zero and the MDE.

blockers.concern: The candidate corpus contains at most 15 listed fixtures, including borderline and previously smoke-tested cases, while the power search permits N = 16. The illustrative N = 14 formula also exceeds the USD 2,500 envelope before positive-control costs.
blockers.why_matters: The selected powered design may be impossible to execute, leaving an unattended run to improvise a smaller and underpowered experiment.
blockers.location: FR-1; FR-6; Risks & Mitigation; Appendix D
blockers.recommendation: Calculate the eligible corpus size and affordable design before selecting N. Specify the outcome when no eligible, affordable design meets power, including an explicitly inconclusive feasibility study rather than a conclusive claim.

blockers.concern: The eligibility, group order, affordable-N fallback, optional third trials, and budget-driven omissions are not fully deterministic, while the document promises every rule precedes its data.
blockers.why_matters: Discretion after smoke results or interim looks can change the analyzed population and undermine pre-registration despite an unchanged document hash.
blockers.location: FR-6; FR-7; FR-8; Scope — Priority order; Risks & Mitigation
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register executable selection, grouping, replacement, omission, and amendment rules. Specify whether deviations invalidate confirmatory status and prohibit outcome-informed changes from retaining the original confirmatory claim.

blockers.concern: The judge sample oversamples several decision categories but does not define inclusion probabilities, weighting, treatment of partial matches, or a complete finding-to-defect candidate universe.
blockers.why_matters: Unweighted agreement and corrected recall or precision can be biased, particularly when credited pairs, near misses, and stray findings occur at very different rates.
blockers.recommendation: Define sampling units and inclusion probabilities, mutually exclusive strata, partial-match rules, and weighted estimators with uncertainty. Ensure missed semantic matches outside citation windows remain eligible for validation.

blockers.concern: The matched arm fixes a rounded session count from one smoke cost ratio; it does not enforce equal actual spending. The floor, cap, and variable session costs can produce substantial imbalance.
blockers.why_matters: The primary result could be described as a comparison at equal dollars while comparing materially different budgets.
blockers.recommendation: Define an actual spending policy and matching tolerance as part of the primary estimand. Report realized imbalance and specify how overshooting sessions are handled. Make the budget-constrained comparison primary if equal dollars is the central claim.

blockers.concern: The model running inside each arm is not stated. `a0_bare_matched` is pinned to Opus 5.5 `--effort high`, but the model used by REVIEW and AUDIT inside `a1_full` and `a1_review_only` is never named (the model-mix constraint only covers the cycle's own agents). Cycle-131 had `a0_bare_fable` as the model control; this cycle drops it. If the pipeline runs Fable 5.1 while bare runs Opus 5.5, the primary contrast confounds 'pipeline vs bare' with 'Fable vs Opus'. `post_cutoff` is also evaluated only against Opus's catalog date.
blockers.why_matters: A Δ that is really a model difference would be attributed to the pipeline, and the report's one-sentence answer would recommend paying for the wrong thing. Conversely a null could hide a pipeline effect cancelled by a model difference. Without the model named per arm the result is uninterpretable and the per-dollar comparison is between unlike things.
blockers.location: FR-3, FR-8, § Constraints 'Model mix', § Technical Considerations 'Dependencies', FR-1 post_cutoff
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register the exact model id per arm and per phase (REVIEW, AUDIT, BARE) and record it in every row. Either run the bare matched arm with the same model the pipeline's reviewer uses, or keep both (matched-Opus and matched-same-model) and declare which one is the primary contrast. Record post_cutoff against every model's availability date that appears in any arm.

blockers.concern: The open-mount control is required to read positive without a defined contrast, effect threshold, uncertainty criterion, or proof that exposure must improve recall on already high-performing fixtures.
blockers.why_matters: Ceiling effects or stochastic variation can void an otherwise valid study, while an unspecified positive result can be interpreted selectively.
blockers.recommendation: Separate verification of oracle accessibility from a statistical lift test. Pre-register the contrast and pass criteria, select suitable control fixtures independently, and evaluate apparatus validity before confirmatory interpretation.

blockers.concern: The power model treats repeated bare catches as independent draws using 1 − (1 − p)^k, although repeated sessions can systematically miss the same defects.
blockers.why_matters: Incorrect dependence assumptions can misestimate matched-arm recall, between-PR variance, required sample size, and the likelihood of a useful result.
blockers.recommendation: Model defect difficulty and dependence between repeated sessions. Use available repeated-run evidence and broad dependence sensitivities; revise the power claim if matched-arm dependence cannot be estimated.

blockers.concern: The power simulation evaluates a fixed-sample cluster-bootstrap test rather than the complete YES, NO, and futility procedure that will determine study termination.
blockers.why_matters: The advertised 80% power does not establish the probability of reaching the intended operational conclusion under the implemented design.
blockers.recommendation: Simulate all looks, exclusions, stopping boundaries, futility decisions, and budget truncation. Report probabilities of each final conclusion across effects below, at, and above the practical threshold.

blockers.concern: The primary recall estimand and pairing structure are not fully specified: equal PR weighting versus pooled defect weighting, aggregation of two trials, shared implementation ancestry, and permutation units are unresolved.
blockers.why_matters: Reasonable implementations can produce different estimates and uncertainty, while related sprint fixtures may supply fewer independent clusters than their PR count suggests.
blockers.recommendation: Define the estimand mathematically, identify the independent sampling unit, document related fixtures, and specify trial aggregation and valid permutation units. Include dependence sensitivity at a broader project or ancestry cluster where feasible.

blockers.concern: The sandbox has network access and the fixtures come from a public repository whose fix commits already sit on `main`. The PRD acknowledges this and relies on the grader's contamination scan, but that scan inspects scratch-directory shapes; it cannot see a `git fetch`, `gh api` or raw HTTPS read of the fix commit that leaves no file behind.
blockers.why_matters: Any arm can read the answer key from GitHub. A matched arm with k sessions has k chances to do so. Contamination of either arm silently biases Δ in an unknown direction and the 'unseen corpus' claim evaporates. The closed mount only protects the local answer paths.
blockers.location: FR-1 contamination_note, § Technical Considerations 'Constraints inherited' (KF-046), FR-5 validity rule 'contaminated null'
blockers.recommendation: Run Phase 1 arms with network egress disabled or restricted to the model API endpoint only; if full egress is unavoidable, log every outbound connection per run (proxy or eBPF capture), scan transcripts for `git fetch`, `gh`, `curl` and the repository URL, and add 'network fetch of repo or fix commit' as a took-effect failure. Pre-register this rule.

blockers.concern: The sandbox retains network access while fixes and feedback are public, and the specification relies on contamination scanning to detect exposure.
blockers.why_matters: A model can retrieve answer material despite closed local mounts, and incomplete access logging can leave contaminated results classified as valid.
blockers.recommendation: Deny unnecessary network access and restrict required egress to model endpoints. Audit tool calls and accessible Git history, remotes, caches, and metadata; treat unavailable exposure evidence as unknown rather than clean.

blockers.concern: The sequential procedure assumes canonical O'Brien–Fleming boundaries apply to bootstrap-standardized recall differences at PR-count fractions, without establishing their joint sampling distribution or actual information fractions.
blockers.why_matters: Small numbers of heterogeneous PRs, estimated bootstrap standard errors, and unequal group information can invalidate the claimed sequential error control.
blockers.recommendation: Specify the spending-function implementation and information measure, then simulate the complete proposed stopping procedure under relevant nulls and heterogeneous PR structures. Validate overall error rates rather than only checking three reference boundary values.

blockers.concern: The specification hashes the pre-registration before Phase 1, but derives k from Phase 1 smoke runs even though the hashed document must already contain k. The power calculation also depends on those costs.
blockers.why_matters: The required order cannot be followed literally and creates an opportunity to alter design choices after observing current-study outcomes.
blockers.location: FR-3; FR-6; FR-7; FR-8; Timeline Sprint 1
blockers.recommendation: Separate a pre-smoke protocol from the final registration. Commit the deterministic smoke-to-k and budget rules first, restrict access to smoke outcome grades during design, then freeze the final design before confirmatory runs.
